experiences.rule: Once per scene, an Experience that materially changes the approach can grant one Edge or permission to attempt a specialized task.

metadata.source: Fifteen legacy prototype legacy personality types, rewritten as voluntary Universal roleplay prompts.
metadata.mechanical_bonus: None unless the player turns a prompt into a Conviction, Tie, Duty, Experience, or Temptation.

rules.choice: Choose one, combine two, write a new profile, or leave the profile open until play reveals it.
rules.alignment: The eight axes record demonstrated costly behavior, not mood or personality.
rules.culture: The community that raised the character supplies habits, etiquette, practices, and expectations without granting biological mechanics.
rules.resolve: A Drive or Blind Spot can create Resolve only after the player writes it as an eligible Conviction, Tie, Duty, or Temptation and accepts a meaningful cost.

profiles.name: Adventurer
profiles.strength: Courage, momentum, and willingness to enter a changing situation.
profiles.blind_spot: Risk before reflection, or treating danger as proof that a choice matters.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Move first and solve the consequences in motion.
axis_questions: Does risk serve others or personal appetite?
When does freedom become lack of restraint?

profiles.name: Diplomat
profiles.drive: Create a relationship or agreement that can survive disagreement.
profiles.blind_spot: Avoiding a necessary confrontation or treating peace as more important than justice.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Search for the unstated need, concession, or shared language.
axis_questions: Is cooperation voluntary?
What promise cannot be traded away?

profiles.name: Enthusiast
profiles.blind_spot: Overcommitment, distraction, or pushing others to match their energy.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Create motion and recruit others into it.
axis_questions: Does excitement respect consent?
What happens when restraint would protect someone?

profiles.name: Guardian
profiles.drive: Keep a person, place, relationship, or duty safe.
profiles.strength: Reliability, care, and endurance under pressure.
profiles.blind_spot: Possessiveness, paternalism, or erasing their own needs.
axis_questions: Does protection preserve autonomy?
When does duty become ownership?

profiles.name: Historian
profiles.drive: Understand how the past produced the present.
profiles.strength: Context, memory, provenance, and recognition of repeating structures.
profiles.blind_spot: Treating precedent as destiny or valuing records above living testimony.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Look for the earlier version of the current crisis.
axis_questions: Which traditions deserve preservation?
Who was excluded from the surviving record?

profiles.name: Innovator
profiles.drive: Make a new answer where none exists.
profiles.blind_spot: Ignoring downstream cost, maintenance, or the consent of those affected.
axis_questions: Is transformation invited or imposed?
Who carries the risk of failure?

profiles.name: Maverick
profiles.strength: Independence, dissent, and resistance to coercion.
profiles.blind_spot: Rejecting help, structure, or responsibility because it resembles control.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Break the assumed rule and choose an unclaimed path.
axis_questions: Is rebellion self-directed or selfish?
Which chosen obligations remain binding?

profiles.name: Mystic
profiles.strength: Intuition, spiritual attention, and comfort with uncertainty.
profiles.blind_spot: Reading intention into coincidence or granting symbols more authority than people.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Listen for the pattern that ordinary senses miss.
axis_questions: Does faith preserve autonomy?
When should a sign be tested rather than obeyed?

profiles.name: Optimist
profiles.drive: Protect the possibility of a better outcome.
profiles.strength: Hope, recovery, and the ability to imagine survival after loss.
profiles.blind_spot: Minimizing danger, grief, anger, or evidence that demands a harder response.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Name the remaining possibility and move toward it.
axis_questions: Does hope require honesty?
Who pays for one more chance?

profiles.name: Perfectionist
profiles.drive: Make the work exact, complete, and dependable.
profiles.strength: Precision, preparation, and detection of weak points.
profiles.blind_spot: Paralysis, control, harsh self-judgment, or treating people as flawed work.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Narrow the problem and remove every uncontrolled variable.
axis_questions: When does discipline become domination?
Can an imperfect repair still be merciful?

profiles.name: Realist
profiles.drive: Work from present evidence and practical limits.
profiles.strength: Grounded judgment, triage, and resistance to wishful thinking.
profiles.blind_spot: Mistaking caution for certainty or treating the current order as inevitable.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Identify what is true, available, and survivable right now.
axis_questions: Does pragmatism preserve honor?
Which possibility is being dismissed too early?

profiles.name: Scholar
profiles.strength: Deep knowledge, disciplined inquiry, and teachable models.
profiles.blind_spot: Neglecting immediate needs, lived expertise, or the politics of knowledge.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Form a question precise enough to answer.
axis_questions: Who controls the archive?
What knowledge should not be used merely because it can be understood?

profiles.name: Strategist
profiles.drive: Shape events before they become crises.
profiles.blind_spot: Treating people as pieces or believing a plan deserves obedience.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Create options, reserves, and an exit before committing.
axis_questions: Does the plan preserve consent?
Which sacrifice is the strategist willing to bear personally?

profiles.name: Traditionalist
profiles.drive: Preserve continuity, ritual, memory, and inherited meaning.
profiles.strength: Stability, stewardship, and knowledge carried through community practice.
profiles.blind_spot: Protecting a harmful custom or confusing age with legitimacy.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Return to the oldest trusted obligation or rite.
axis_questions: Which traditions were chosen and which were imposed?
What must change so the valuable part can survive?

profiles.name: Visionary
profiles.drive: Build toward a future others cannot yet see.
profiles.strength: Direction, imagination, and coalition around possibility.
profiles.blind_spot: Leaving details, repair, dissent, or consent behind.
profiles.pressure_pattern: Reframe the crisis as the first step of a larger transformation.
axis_questions: Who chose the future being built?
What is preserved during transformation?

derived.hit_points: class hit die at level 1 + Constitution modifier; later levels use class average or roll
derived.composure: 8 + PB + greater of Wisdom or Charisma modifier
derived.initiative: Dexterity test; Breakthrough grants favorable opening
derived.speed: 30 feet by default, modified only by class features, equipment, conditions, or a campaign-specific rule
derived.carry: 10 + Strength score in abstract slots unless a module uses mass

origin_and_community.rule: Race, optional bloodline or form, body description, community, language, and personal history are related but separate fields. Race establishes physiology and listed fictional permissions or limits; it never dictates morality, class, personality, or compulsory religion.
origin_and_community.campaign_defined_forms: Campaigns may add local cultures, mixed communities, body variations, and off-world adaptations without erasing the selected race record. Any new numerical feature must be explicit rather than inferred from appearance.
required_questions: Which race profile does the character use?
Does that race offer a bloodline or form, and which one was selected?
Where did the character grow up?
What languages or communication systems do they use?
What parts of their body or presentation matter to the player?
Which listed race limitations matter in this campaign, and how will the table handle them safely?

race_selection.choose_one_race: Choose one race profile at character creation. Select a listed bloodline or form only when the race provides one.
race_selection.no_fixed_ability_scores: Race never grants a fixed ability-score increase, alignment, class, personality, or compulsory religion.
race_selection.physiology_and_permissions: Body, abilities, and limitations establish anatomy and fictional permissions. Use normal tests when an outcome is uncertain; a race entry does not silently add numerical bonuses unless a future option explicitly says so.
race_selection.limitations_are_not_point_flaws: Listed limitations are real fictional constraints and safety-relevant setting facts. They do not award Background Build Points or XP.
race_selection.culture_is_separate: The society text is a common cultural pattern, not mandatory behavior. Community, upbringing, language, and personal history remain separate character choices.
race_selection.deity_associations: Homeworld deity links are public religious and cultural associations. They are not biological ownership, compulsory worship, or proof that one Architect solely created a race.
race_selection.alien_deity_scope: The attached assignment index intentionally does not assign the off-world Alien-Folk to Universalian deities.
